title: Harnessing Conventional Video Processing Insights for Emerging 3D Video Generation Models: A Comprehensive Attention-aware Way
problem: 3D video generation models with full attention mechanisms incur >75% of compute in attention operations, causing high inference latency and energy consumption.
motivation: Video generation requires full attention across spatial-temporal dimensions; exploiting token similarities (analogous to patch compression in video codecs) can reduce compute.
method: Proposes SimPicker, a co-design combining algorithm and hardware: (1) speculation-based similarity exploitation at frame level (coarse) and token level (fine); (2) buffered lookup-table multiplier for FP-INT operations; (3) adaptive grouping strategy to handle workload imbalance from randomly distributed similar tokens.
key_novelty: Speculation-based similarity detection and FP-INT LUT multiplication architecture for efficient 3D video attention.
contributions: Coarse- and fine-grained similarity exploitation algorithm with dynamic adaptation
LUT-based FP-INT multiplier architecture reducing bank conflicts
5.21x-1.45x speedup vs A100 GPU; 17.92x-1.63x energy efficiency vs state-of-the-art accelerators
limitations: Not discussed—focus on algorithm-hardware co-design without addressing generalization to other attention-based models.
primary_theme: Similarity-aware attention acceleration for 3D video generation
